text: 最近，一位“洛丽塔”女孩引起了不小的议论。
en: Recently, a 'Lolita' girl has sparked quite a discussion.

text: 不到160的身高，体重近200斤。
en: Under 160 cm tall, weighing nearly 200 jin.

text: 她非常喜欢穿“洛丽塔”，隔段时间就会买一套新衣服。
en: She loves wearing 'Lolita' very much, and buys a new outfit every so often.

text: 然后，在社交平台上晒出自己的“美照”。
en: Then she posts her 'beautiful photos' on social platforms.

text: 最开始，大家并没有很在意是不是真的“卡哇伊”，只是担心她的健康。
en: At first, people did not care much whether she was really 'kawaii'; they were just worried about her health.

text: 有人建议她减肥，有人建议她体检。
en: Some suggested she lose weight; others suggested she get a check-up.

text: 没想到，她直接将“只接受夸奖，不接受批评”写在简介上。
en: Unexpectedly, she wrote directly in her bio: 'Only compliments accepted, no criticism'.

text: 但胖不胖是她自己的事，我们夸不夸是我们的事。
en: But whether she is fat or not is her business, and whether we compliment her or not is ours.

text: 所以有网友这样说：
en: So one netizen said this:

text: “我觉得，就是要实话实说啊。
en: “I think we should just tell the truth.

text: 如果一味地夸赞，就会让人觉得这就是美、就是好看的方式。
en: If you just keep praising, people will think this is beauty, this is the way to look good.

text: 这样久了会慢慢的变得扭曲，实话实说才好吧。
en: Over time it slowly becomes distorted; telling the truth is better, isn't it.

text: “美的确没有定义，但是实话就是真的胖啊。
en: “Beauty indeed has no definition, but the truth is she really is fat.

text: 眼看辩驳无力，她又开始用探讨美的标准来逃避，并冠以自信等词语。
en: Seeing she could not win the argument, she began using discussions of beauty standards to dodge, dressing it up with words like confidence.

text: “现在满大街的瘦子和普通体型的全是亚健康，难道胖子就要十全十美？
en: “Nowadays the skinny people and average builds all over the street are all subhealthy — must fat people be perfect in every way?

text: “身为年轻人，我仅仅是跑不动步，爬不动楼梯，却要在我身上无限放大。
en: “As a young person, I merely cannot run or climb stairs, yet everything about me gets infinitely magnified.

text: 于是，评论区便有了这样的略带浮夸的赞美：
en: So the comments section had this kind of slightly exaggerated praise:

text: 太漂亮了，再胖点会更好看哦。
en: So beautiful! Getting a bit fatter would look even better.

text: 做自己就好，生活是活给自己看的，晚上要多加两个汉堡跟可乐，开心最重要。
en: Just be yourself; life is lived for yourself. Have two more burgers and a cola at night — being happy matters most.

text: 如果是120斤左右，可能都不会有人说胖。
en: If she were around 120 jin, probably no one would call her fat.

text: 如果接受不了议论，完全可以选择仅自己可见。
en: If you cannot take discussion, you can simply choose to make it visible only to yourself.

text: 可她偏偏选择了“流量”最大的方式。
en: But she chose the way that gets the most 'traffic'.

text: 我很反感那种无脑攻击别人的人，但是也反感那种明明不好。
en: I really dislike people who mindlessly attack others, but I also dislike people who are clearly not good.

text: 却硬生生的给自己创造了一个信息茧房，只准夸的人。
en: Yet stubbornly build themselves an information cocoon that only allows praise.

text: 有时在网上会被一些人的言论惊讶到，我就会疑惑，为什么会说出这么没常识的话？
en: Sometimes I am surprised by what people say online, and I wonder: how can they say something so lacking in common sense?

text: 后来想一想，可能这就是大数据造就的信息茧房。
en: Later I thought about it: maybe this is the information cocoon created by big data.

text: 就像曾经很有名气的方舟子，只要碰到意见不同的人就拉黑。
en: Take Fang Zhouzi, who was once very famous: whenever he met someone with a different opinion, he blocked them.

text: 最近他发文说自己拉黑了14万人。
en: Recently he posted that he has blocked 140,000 people.

text: 我算了一下，即使每天拉黑100个人，也得需要整整4年。
en: I did the math: even blocking 100 people a day would take a full 4 years.

text: 人是怎么越来越偏激的，看这位就够了，自己给自己造了一个巨大的信息茧房。
en: To see how a person becomes more and more extreme, this example is enough: he built himself a huge information cocoon.

text: 他们生活在自认为正确的观点里，我们很难借助外在信息来向他们证明。
en: They live inside views they think are correct, and it is hard for us to prove otherwise using outside information.

text: 比如“饭圈文化”，专门追星的小圈子。
en: Take 'fan-circle culture', for example — small circles dedicated to chasing stars.

text: 时间越长就会越来越“排外”，拉踩行为无处不在，一言不合就爆粗口。
en: The longer it goes on, the more 'exclusive' it becomes; trampling rivals is everywhere, and a single disagreement brings swearing.

text: 可怕的是，这种现象，不只是在那些追星的群体上得以体现。
en: What is frightening is that this phenomenon is not only reflected in those star-chasing groups.

text: 在茧房中，信息相互屏蔽，人们在自说自话中固化认知。
en: Inside the cocoon, information blocks each other off, and people solidify their cognition while talking to themselves.

text: 更甚者，演变成群情激愤的互喷，可绝大多数人，很难意识到这一点。
en: Worse, it escalates into furious mutual attacks, yet the vast majority of people can hardly realise this.

text: 但很多时候，我们没有主动选择“信息茧房”，也会被困在其中。
en: But often, even when we do not actively choose an 'information cocoon', we still get trapped in one.

text: 比如，长辈们总喜欢转发各种各样的谣言。
en: For example, elders always love forwarding all kinds of rumours.

text: 有时候，我自己辟谣都辟累了，但他们依旧沉迷其中。
en: Sometimes I get tired of debunking them myself, but they remain obsessed.

text: 后来看了爷爷的手机才知道，长辈们已经被“谣言”花式包围。
en: It was only after looking at my grandfather's phone that I realised the elders have been surrounded by 'rumours' in fancy forms.

text: 朋友圈、微信群都充斥着这些信息。
en: Moments and WeChat groups are full of this information.

text: 只要老人家打开手机，总有一条谣言能进入他的视线。
en: As long as an elderly person opens their phone, there will always be a rumour entering their sight.

text: 久而久之，便将自身桎梏“茧房”，堵塞了本应获取信息的渠道。
en: Over time, they imprison themselves in a 'cocoon', blocking the channels through which they should obtain information.

text: 但其实，我们年轻人又何尝不是？
en: But actually, are we young people any different?

text: 在大数据时代，如果你喜欢娱乐搞笑，那么给你推荐的都是各种八卦。
en: In the big data era, if you like entertainment and comedy, you get recommended all kinds of gossip.

text: 如果你喜欢社会热点，那么你每天都能体会一遍世间百态。
en: If you like social hot topics, you can experience the whole range of human life every day.

text: 如果不去主动搜索，软件中永远不会出现学习增长类的信息。
en: If you do not actively search, learning and growth content will never appear in the apps.

text: 每天看的东西，都是大数据根据喜好推送的，被动习惯的接受后。
en: What you see every day is pushed according to your preferences by big data, and after passively and habitually accepting it.

text: 久而久之仿佛是一张看不见的网，将我们束缚在原地，不能接触和了解更多新的东西。
en: Over time it is like an invisible net, binding us in place, unable to contact and understand more new things.

text: 你看到的，永远都是自己想看到的。
en: What you see is always only what you want to see.

text: 你学到的，永远都是你认同的那些观点。
en: What you learn is always only the views you agree with.

text: 你听到的，永远都是你想听的那些声音。
en: What you hear is always only the voices you want to hear.

text: 长此以往，便带来一个非常可怕的后果：你从此丧失了全面看待事物的能力。
en: In the long run, this brings a very terrible consequence: you lose the ability to see things comprehensively.

text: 你看到的，也许都是你赞同的信息，但绝非世界的本来面目。
en: What you see may all be information you agree with, but it is by no means the world as it really is.

text: 比如，有网友患有抑郁症，大数据以为他喜欢这方面的信息。
en: For example, a netizen suffers from depression, and big data thinks he likes this kind of information.

text: 源源不断的推荐这方面的东西，却一度让他产生“厌世”情绪。
en: It keeps recommending such things, which once made him feel 'world-weary'.

text: 如果我们不主动去看书、去阅读，去搜索信息。
en: If we do not actively read books, read, and search for information.

text: 那么我们就只能知道，自己想知道的事情，或者已经知道的事情。
en: Then we can only know what we want to know, or what we already know.

text: 生活在互联网时代，如果我们觉得网络的观点与我们的观点一致。
en: Living in the internet age, if we feel that online views agree with our views.

text: 不是因为我们有多聪明，而是因为我们太笨了。
en: It is not because we are so smart, but because we are too foolish.

text: 不懂得去主动搜寻自己不知道的事情，所以一直封闭在自己的角落。
en: Not knowing how to actively search for things we do not know, we stay closed in our own corner.

text: 而网络看似给我们提供了不少信息，实际上也无形给我们加了一道壁垒。
en: And the internet, while seemingly providing us with a lot of information, has also invisibly added a barrier for us.

text: 心理学上，曾提到过两种认知偏差：朴素现实主义和朴素犬儒主义。
en: In psychology, two cognitive biases have been mentioned: naive realism and naive cynicism.

text: “朴素现实主义”的人，总相信自己掌握真理，他人是不理性，甚至有偏见的。
en: A 'naive realism' person always believes they grasp the truth, while others are irrational or even biased.

text: 而“朴素犬儒主义”的人，总认为自己是客观的，他人在以自我为中心。
en: A 'naive cynicism' person always thinks they are objective, while others are self-centred.

text: 这两种都是典型的窄化视野，为自己筑造信息茧房。
en: Both are typical narrow vision, building an information cocoon for oneself.

text: 长期只吃自己喜欢的某一种食物，会营养不良的。
en: Eating only one kind of food you like for a long time will cause malnutrition.

text: 同样，长期只看自己喜欢的信息，也会让自己包容性下降。
en: Similarly, only reading information you like for a long time will reduce your tolerance.

text: 其实，正常的价值观体系，会在一个大框架里有小范围波动的。
en: Actually, a normal value system fluctuates within a small range inside a large framework.

text: 如果一成不变，那证明你一直没有接触到新的信息，也没有任何主动的思考。
en: If it never changes, that proves you have never encountered new information, nor done any active thinking.

text: 比如有网友偶然认识一个级别非常高的大佬，她每次讲那么一点点，网友都觉得受益匪浅。
en: For example, a netizen happened to meet a very high-level big shot; every little bit he said, the netizen felt greatly benefited.

text: 因为他讲的这些，是普通人根本不会接触到的信息。
en: Because what he said was information ordinary people would never encounter.

text: 但实际上，信息就在那里，只是我们不去主动寻找，也就永远看不到。
en: But actually, the information is right there; it is just that we do not actively seek it, so we never see it.

text: 所以，我们要主动创造一个信息潮，去接触不同的信息。
en: So we must actively create an information tide, to encounter different information.

text: 听多了赞美者的声音，也要去听一下批评的声音。
en: Having heard many voices of praise, you should also listen to voices of criticism.

text: 同一个事件，尝试从不同的角度、不同的群体去获取信息。
en: For the same event, try to obtain information from different angles and different groups.

text: 不同的平台、不同知识层面的人，或许会给你带来意想不到的信息增量。
en: Different platforms and people of different knowledge levels may bring you unexpected information gains.

text: 而愿意了解更多信息的人，可以根据信息内容，自由作出选择。
en: And people willing to learn more information can freely choose based on the information content.

text: 不需要正确，不需要引导，就能建立在信息基础上的自由意志。
en: No need for correctness, no need for guidance, and free will can be built on the basis of information.

text: 而自由意志的前提就是足够多的信息，在不了解事实的情况下，人其实并没有自由意志。
en: And the premise of free will is enough information; without understanding the facts, a person actually has no free will.

text: 了解越深层次的事实，人就会越智慧，慈悲，平和待人。
en: The deeper you understand the facts, the wiser, more compassionate and more peaceful you become toward others.

text: 这不是教导出来的正确观念，而是见多识广之后，自然呈现的生命状态。
en: This is not a correct concept taught to you, but a state of life that naturally emerges after seeing much and knowing much.

text: 尼采曾说，我们的认知边界，就是我们世界的边界。
en: Nietzsche once said: the boundaries of our cognition are the boundaries of our world.

text: 所以我们要尽可能的多走多看多听，毕竟命运会区别对待认知水平不同的人。
en: So we should walk more, see more and listen more; after all, fate treats people of different cognitive levels differently.

text: 共勉！
en: Let us encourage each other!
